source.author: verg
source.text: hunc cape consiliis socium et coniunge volentem; huic trade, amissis superant qui navibus, et quos pertaesum magni incepti rerumque tuarum est; longaevosque senes ac fessas aequore matres, et quidquid tecum invalidum metuensque pericli est, delige, et his habeant terris sine moenia fessi:
source.text_original: hunc cape consiliis socium et coniunge volentem; / huic trade, amissis superant qui navibus, et quos / pertaesum magni incepti rerumque tuarum est; / longaevosque senes ac fessas aequore matres, / et quidquid tecum invalidum metuensque pericli est, / delige, et his habeant terris sine moenia fessi: /
source.text_english: Take him as a partner in your plans and join him willingly; entrust to him those who survive the lost ships, and those who are wearied of the great undertaking and of your affairs; and the long-lived old men and the mothers tired by the sea, and whatever among you is feeble and fearful of danger, choose them out, and let these weary ones have walls here on these lands:

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: non degeneres, ut reris, Acaste, venimus ad questus: socium te iungere coeptis est animus; neque enim Telamon aut Canthus et Idas Tyndareusque puer mihi vellere dignior Helles.
reuse.text_original: 'non degeneres, ut reris, Acaste, / venimus ad questus: socium te iungere coeptis / est animus; neque enim Telamon aut Canthus et Idas / Tyndareusque puer mihi vellere dignior Helles.
reuse.text_english: We have not come to complaints, Acaste, in a spirit unworthy, as you think; my purpose is to join you as a companion in my undertakings. For no Telamon, nor Canthus, nor Idas, nor the young Tyndareus, was more worthy for me to pluck the Hellespont.
